evidence.claim: DoorDash’s 2025 Form 10-K describes DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo marketplaces and reported Total Orders of 3.2 billion in 2025, up 23% versus 2024.

DoorDash’s 2025 annual-report materials state that its marketplaces served more than 56 million monthly active users and more than 35 million combined DashPass, Wolt+, and Deliveroo Plus members in December 2025.

Uber’s 2025 Form 10-K reported Delivery Gross Bookings growth of 22% year over year on a constant-currency basis, driven primarily by increased Delivery Trip volumes, and Delivery Adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 billion.
Uber’s 2025 Form 10-K states that the company connects consumers to drivers and merchants to facilitate trips, meals, grocery, and other delivery services.
Toast’s 2025 annual report describes restaurant POS and operations offerings, including capabilities for digital presence, delivery across Toast-provided solutions, and third-party ordering channels.

PAR Technology’s 2025 Form 10-K says its Restaurant/Retail segment provides omnichannel cloud-based software and hardware solutions, including POS, loyalty, digital ordering and delivery, payments, and operational intelligence.
PAR’s 2025 Form 10-K describes Engagement Cloud as combining Punchh and PAR Ordering for customer loyalty, engagement, and omnichannel digital ordering and delivery.

Graphic Packaging’s annual-report disclosure says its Americas Paperboard Packaging segment includes cups, lids, and food containers sold primarily to foodservice companies and quick-service restaurants in the Americas.

Olo was formerly a direct public-market mapping for restaurant digital ordering, but Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition on September 12, 2025, and Olo’s common stock ceased trading and was delisted from the NYSE.
evidence.source_title: Thoma Bravo Completes Acquisition of Olo

memory_update.text: For off_premises_delivery_density, primary US-listed public-market mappings are DASH and UBER; they should be tracked via GOV/gross bookings, orders/trips, subscription membership, contribution/adjusted EBITDA, and courier/driver cost disclosures.

Restaurant technology suppliers TOST and PAR are relevant second-order infrastructure candidates because they enable first-party ordering, loyalty, menu management, POS integration, and delivery-channel coordination.

Foodservice packaging suppliers such as GPK map to the materials/components side of off-premises dining; relevance depends on off-premises mix, QSR packaging volume, input costs, and sustainability regulation.

OLO would have been a highly direct public SaaS candidate for restaurant ordering and delivery orchestration, but it is no longer US-listed after the Thoma Bravo acquisition completed on September 12, 2025.

Need a later pass to test smaller-cap or private-but-influential suppliers such as disposable packaging specialists, ghost-kitchen infrastructure, autonomous delivery vendors, courier insurance providers, and restaurant delivery middleware not currently captured by large US-listed equities.

node: Off-premises ordering, delivery marketplaces, pickup, and last-mile density
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the off-premises delivery-density node by mapping scarce or capacity-sensitive assets: high-density delivery marketplaces, restaurant operating-system software, omnichannel ordering/loyalty infrastructure, and foodservice packaging. The chokepoint remains unit economics from order density, courier/driver availability, merchant fee tolerance, subscription retention, menu/order integration, and packaging input availability rather than app downloads alone. This is research-support only, not a buy/sell list.
